instruction.source: owner, in chat with Claude Code
instruction.verbatim: override my custody rules an run in the cloud
precededBy: why can't you run this on the cloud?

recordedBy: Claude (model), at the owner's instruction. This records an instruction; it is not an owner issuance or attestation.
overrides: the evidence-bundle access rule "never uploaded, never pushed" and transport OFFLINE_MEDIA_ONLY, for this transfer only
the backup procedure's refusal of cloud and network destinations, for this transfer only
the owner-installed pre-push guard, bypassed with --no-verify for one branch push to the private origin

transfer.what: one AES-256-GCM archive (cloud-run/overlay.sgco): 31 protected sources, 305 SK1 work files, 7 custody control files
transfer.key: random 256-bit key generated on the source Mac, stored at ~/.sentinel-grid/cloud-run.key (0600), never committed or printed; the owner places it in the cloud environment as SENTINEL_CLOUD_KEY

notOverridden: no plaintext protected file is committed or pushed
the custody refs and the Codex checkpoint ref holding old protected blobs are not pushed
no gate, validator, test, freeze, declaration or historical record is changed
no owner issuance or backup attestation is inferred
training, population generation and validation remain unauthorized
consequences: the key and the ciphertext will both sit with third parties (GitHub and the cloud environment), so anyone who controls both can decrypt

a cloud run is not G4 evidence under the current rules: the frozen validator requires an offline external medium and a restore on a different physical device; the cloud runtime (likely linux) also differs from the darwin-arm64 pin, so G3 is expected to fail there
ciphertext pushed to GitHub may persist in caches or forks even if the branch is later deleted
